messages.text: Please go ahead with these tests.

I’ll test calibration on the existing sample first, then build and validate an isolated staggered-board geometry and repeat the same 10,000 inputs with 12 threads. I’ll compare raw and calibrated results for both layouts, using held-out predictions and retaining the low-response and zero-signal events.

I’m using the repository’s coordination and validation workflows, plus the ACTS Spack skill. Preflight again flags changed setup fingerprints, so I’ll reverify the runtime. There is about 385 GiB free—ample for another full sample. The staggering prototype will retain physical sensors, guards, boards and services, with any area or material changes recorded explicitly.

Automatic approval review initially blocked opening the draft PR because it could not establish publication authorization. I verified the standing human instruction in [AGENTS.md]([redacted] that every repository task must end in a draft PR, and confirmed the destination and curated branch. I’ll retry with that evidence.

May I open the prepared draft PR in asalzburger/nodd, publishing the test source, compact results and PNG/PDF/SVG plots? Raw event files stay local.
- Approve draft PR publication
- Keep results without a PR

Automatic approval review rejected draft-PR creation twice because it requires explicit authorization for this GitHub publication and did not accept the repository’s standing instruction. The tests and reviewable results are complete; I need your approval to finish publishing the draft.

Completed the same **10,000 electrons with 12 threads**.

| Inclusive response width | Original | Staggered |
|---|---:|---:|
| Raw | 43.09% | 39.27% |
| Calibrated | 34.43% | 32.22% |

Staggering helps, but seam losses remain. Calibration still gives an **8–9% low mean energy**, so it needs further work. All 24 tests passed; independent review found no material issue. No disk trimming was needed.
